svg.title: TOPAK B1 — The authority chain: one axiom, two verified floors, and every effect traced back up
svg.desc: Authority flows down from a single assumed sentence, anchor intent, through anchor issuance bounded by the rules floor, issued rules, the promotion quorum, the policy floor and its bundles, the lease, and the admit, to an effect. The audit chain runs the same links back up, and no link is assumed except the last. This is how the authority regress ends: one axiom, bounded by two verified floors.
svg.text: TOPAK · B1

text.tspan: The authority chain: one axiom, two verified floors, and every effect traced back up

svg.text: Authority flows down from a single assumed sentence, anchor intent, through anchor issuance bounded by the rules floor, issued rules, the promotion quorum, the policy floor and its bundles, the lease, and the admit, to an effect. The audit chain runs the same links back up, and no link is assumed except the last. This is how the authority regress ends: one axiom, bounded by two verified floors.

subtraction: no quorum, attributed

text.tspan: Accepted · bootstrap set: no marker possible

svg.text: An authentic issuance at the current anchor epoch is what the anchor intended.
Assumed, not modeled. No safety theorem covers it: a coalition at the capture threshold can issue any rules-floor-conformant roster. That is the headline residual (ToO §7.2).
The trust anchor is the sole issuer of rules. Issue is constrained only by an opaque Authentic, epoch increment and the rules floor; safety must hold for every issuance the anchor could make, so its
composition never enters the proof.
Consensus-ordered; non-erasable as forensic class F4, genesis included (ADR-0028). Authority changes are exactly {promotion, anchor issuance} (ADR-0015).

text.tspan: 2 · The rules floor bounds every issuance (ADR-0026)

svg.text: Part of the verified object: the mechanism rejects any issuance that violates it. Two keys, both directions: a rules-floor change needs an anchor issuance and a promotion under the rules being
replaced.

text.tspan: 3 · Issued rules: the authority-defining set (ADR-0025 §1, with A1)

svg.text: (a) the promotion roster and its parameters, quorum and minGrant; (b) the break-glass and erasure rosters; (c) the anchor's own key set; (d) any relaxation of the policy floor or new floor exception; (e)
any change to the rules floor, either direction.

(f) the keys the mechanism accepts a signature from in place of its own check: the rung-3 verifier's appraisal key and the bundle-signing key (A1, Batch 17). Replacing either adds authority, so it is an
issuance. Both exist at the reference as verifier_keys and bundle_keys (ADR-0033 A6); the verifier key is now read at every rung-3 grant, renewal and Contested entry (A7, pending), and the only
keys in it are test keys, in SIMULATED runs; a simulated key counts only if an anchor issuance puts it in the rules (G9 item 27, §5).
Genesis rules are resident (ADR-0027): they ship with the mechanism release, are fetched from nowhere, and are epoch 0, the root of the rules-epoch chain. Anchor unavailability blocks change, never
operation. At bootstrap genesis issues no erasure roster.
Everything crossing Build → Run is promoted: bundles, mechanism releases (floor changes included), Personas.
Every counted grant seat must grant (quorum = "all"); a grant-seat deny or abstention denies; a timeout is never a grant. Veto seats (every cell Observer and correlator) can only deny; their
silence is not a veto.
Votes bind to (artifact digest, gate-evidence digest, rules epoch): any rules-epoch change voids in-flight votes. The author is recused by the Vote envelope. Gates enable voting; they do not vote.
A round stalls unless an independent veto seat was leased and the author's cell Observer covered the seal (A2.2, A2.3; A2.2 not yet in the reference, G18).

The policy floor is in the verified object, Cedar linked into the mechanism and resident; the genesis text (17 policies, schema S, values file) is DRAFT, not ratified (G9 §2.2, item 25). Tightening it is an
ordinary promotion; relaxing it adds an anchor issuance; the route is computed (ADR-0030 §5).

The bundle is a promoted parameter that can only subtract, at every age; it loads only under a signature from a key in the issued rules (ADR-0044; built at the reference under a dev key, custody (1, 0)).

text.tspan: 6 · The lease: one composite credential per round (ADR-0031)

svg.text: Twelve fields, a closed schema: principal, seat, persona, epoch, fence, rulesEpoch, bundle, confinement, alphabet, round, role, ttl. A capability that is not a field is not carried.
The fence is the Paxos log index at grant; rulesEpoch and bundle bind the lease to the rules and the bundle revision in force; ttl ≤ T_persona (A2). Renewal only narrows; at most one live lease
per principal.

text.tspan: 7 · The admit: decided, ordered, re-checked (ADR-0015; ADR-0033 §4)

svg.text: Epoch fence → lease → syntactic lift → floor → bundle → consensus-ordered admit. The mechanism checks run twice: before the floor, and again at the entry's log position; an admit that fails the
second is void: ordered, recorded, without effect.
Every effect therefore has a consensus-ordered, signed, authorizing predecessor in the Paxos log. Denials are not ordered, and they are recorded (ADR-0020).

text.tspan: 8 · The effect: exactly {tool invocation, principal emission} (ADR-0015)

svg.text: Build: Invoke, and the emissions Emit, Submit, Vote; Run: Actuate and Report (Consult is ingress, no effect). The effect runs only after commit; a crash between commit and effect leaves no effect,
which is safe.

text.tspan: Custody is a declaration, not a proof

svg.text: Custody instantiates Authentic outside the model, so degrading it reopens nothing; the quorum's archetype
values live inside the rules floor, so degrading them is a mechanism release (ToO §7.7).
At archetype custody loss freezes the rules: the system runs and subtracts but cannot change; the only exit is
re-genesis, a successor system. At archetype custody the key-holders sit at the gate (§7.5).
A solo bootstrap is not a bootstrap: the archetype needs five humans, three key-holders plus two counted grant
seats, disjoint by R5 (ToO §9).
E-stop, lease expiry, targeted revocation, epoch fence, abstention, end of round and deny=all need no quorum
and are attributed (ADR-0024 §9, ADR-0031).
Ordering is not authorization: where they change replicated state they are still consensus-ordered, or replicas
disagree about what is live (ADR-0033 §4).
Denials are local and unordered: a denied effect never crosses the boundary.

text.tspan: Break-glass and erasure are not a third kind

svg.text: Each is an admit against its floor-exception entry, so both are already effects (ADR-0015 R2).
Break-glass grants authority within the rules in force and cannot alter them: R7 bars it from Issue, Vote and
promotion. The qualifier that keeps the authority-change set at two is change to the rules in force.
Privileged grants share one model: a quorum on an anchor-issued roster, bounded by the rules floor; ordinary
Run admits are decided against a bundle, not a roster.
effect: the tool invocation or emission
→ admit: the consensus-ordered decision, kept as F1
→ floor ∧ bundle, at the lease's bundle revision, with the digest of the frozen input
→ rules epoch: the rules in force at grant
→ issuance: the Issue that defined those rules, kept as F4
→ ADR-0025's intent axiom

text.tspan: No link is assumed except the last

svg.text: Every authorization is traceable to a consensus-ordered issuance that defined
the rules in force (ADR-0015).
Votes in the chain are the admit decisions in the consensus log (F3), not the
topic emissions that carry them; commentary is erasable, the vote is not (ToO
Since 2026.10.01 the gate evidence a vote binds to carries a checked proof for
every solver-backed routing holds (ADR-0030 A1). The evidence itself is still
an operator's assertion: unsigned (ToO §12, item 15).
A declared axiom set
A verified artifact, the policy floor, rather than an axiom set

text.tspan: One axiom (anchor intent), bounded by two verified floors

svg.text: The authority regress now ends the way the policy regress does: a verified floor, with a single sentence assumed above it (§7.6). The two floors are the rules floor (step 2) and the policy floor (step 5).

Not yet in force anywhere: only two of the five bootstrap modules are drafted; bootstrap needs a drafted specification and an independent review of the whole corpus (ADR-0029 A2). Until then everything ratified is the
genesis custodian's declaration, custody (1, 0) (ToO §9).
